pull_request.body: **In one sentence:** Command-line tools that read remote volumes (the renderer `vc_render_tifxyz` and the tracer `vc_grow_seg_from_seed`) now respect the same remote-cache disk budget as the VC3D app, so batch runs cannot fill the disk. **Why / where this is useful:** anyone batch-rendering from remote volumes on fixed-size disks (cloud machines, containers, CI) can bound the cache with the VC3D settings from the app's settings dialog. Like the example I ran in to below, I believe that others may have jobs fail as a result of the current state. This fix helps make the codebase more consistent, regardless of where users run the tools. **One real example:** Starting with 66-layer surface-volume renders of scroll windings from an open-data S3 volume (`vc_render_tifxyz --volume ...`) on 50 GB cloud machines, I let a batch run, and `~/.VC3D/remote_cache/` grew to 50 GB in about 2.5 hours on three machines; later renders, and the jobs reading their output, failed with write errors. **Before:** #1170 added `PersistentZarrCacheBudget` (eviction by a maximum size and a free-space floor; #2166 later made the eviction asynchronous), but only the VC3D app configures it (`VCAppMain.cpp`, from `perf/remote_cache_max_gib` and `perf/remote_cache_min_free_gib`). Command-line tools never configure a budget, so `RemoteFileCache` keeps every fetched chunk. **After this PR:** - The two settings' keys and defaults move to `vc/core/util/RemoteCacheSettings.hpp` (next to `remote_cache_delta3d`); `VCSettings.hpp` aliases them, as it already does for `REMOTE_CACHE_DELTA3D`. No behaviour change in the app. - New `vc::settings::configureRemoteCacheBudget()` reads the same keys from the same VC3D.ini and configures the budget for `remoteCachePath()`; it reuses a budget already configured for that root. - `vc_render_tifxyz` and `vc_grow_seg_from_seed` call it before opening a remote volume (one call each). Defaults are the app's: no size cap, keep 20 GiB free. - Same root cause in both tools: each opens remote volumes through `Volume::NewFromUrl`, which caches fetched chunks under `remoteCachePath()` and applies a `PersistentZarrCacheBudget` only if one is configured for that root (`Volume.cpp`, the `findForPath` check); neither tool configured one. **Proof:** the same three real windings (66 layers each, from an open-data S3 volume), each build with its own empty cache folder; cache size sampled every 5 s during each render and measured after it: | build, same VC3D.ini (`remote_cache_max_gib=1`) | peak during render 1 / 2 / 3 | after render 3 | render times | |---|---|---|---| | stock main (budget ignored) | 2,345 / 6,149 / 11,737 MB | 12 GB | 175 s, 267 s, 379 s | | this PR | 1,019 / 1,019 / 1,019 MB | 1,017 MB | 176 s, 281 s, 387 s | Both builds ran back to back in one job with identical settings and inputs. The cache never went over the cap, also during a render, and all six renders succeeded with similar times. Second scroll: the same test on PHerc. 343’s published meshes (1 GB limit) gave the same result. Without this PR the cache grew to 4.3–4.6 GB; with it, it stayed at about 1 GB. - [X] I personally verified that the example and proof above were produced by this PR on the stated data. ## Details - **Tested commit:** this branch on villa main 6aec908a8 (it merges cleanly onto main 322cb0899, 2026-10-24): builds (Release, GCC 13, Ubuntu 24.04), including both `vc_render_tifxyz` and `vc_grow_seg_from_seed`; the new `test_remote_cache_budget_settings` (VC3D.ini in a temporary `VC3D_CONFIG_DIR` → budget registered for the cache root with the configured limits; a second call reuses it) and the existing `test_remote_file_cache` (9 cases) pass. - **Evidence per tool:** the renderer is measured end to end above. The tracer uses the same open path and the same helper, so the renderer's measurement applies to it; it is verified here by build and by the helper's unit test. - **To reproduce (public data, no GPU; ~6 GB free disk; run once with stock main, once with this branch):** ```bash git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Nieuwlaar/pherc343-first-letters # published PHerc. 343 meshes VOL=https://vesuvius-challenge-open-data.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/PHerc0343/volumes/20250521140437-8.640um-1.2m-116keV-masked.zarr rm -rf cfg cache out && mkdir -p cfg cache out printf '[viewer]\nremote_cache_dir=%s\n[perf]\nremote_cache_max_gib=1\nremote_cache_min_free_gib=0\n' "$PWD/cache" > cfg/VC3D.ini for m in w047_R5B2_z9500-11000 w048_R5B2_z9500-11000 concat_w047-w048_R5B2_z9500-11000; do VC3D_CONFIG_DIR=$PWD/cfg QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen vc_render_tifxyz --volume "$VOL" \ --segmentation pherc343-first-letters/outputs/$m.tifxyz --group-idx 0 --scale 1 \ --num-slices 66 --slice-step 1 --auto-crop --cache-gb 4 --zarr-output out/$m.zarr du -sh cache # stock main: 4.3 / 4.6 / 4.6 GB in our run; this branch: ~1 GB each time done ``` - **Limitations:** - The renderer and the tracer apply the budget here. `FiberTraceEvaluationCli` has its own cache-root option and is left for a follow-up; `vc_zarr_download_region` and `vc_zarr_download_bench` deliberately fill the cache and should not evict. - The free-space floor reacts to the whole disk, so other programs filling the same disk also trigger eviction; the size cap (`remote_cache_max_gib`) is the dependable control on shared disks. - The budget comes from VC3D.ini, as in the app; a command-line flag would make batch use easier to script. - The VC3D app keeps its existing code path (it reads the same keys through QSettings); switching it to the new helper as well would remove the second reader, and is left out to keep this PR small and the app unchanged. - **How this was built:** found while rendering at scale with AI assistance (Claude Opus 5.5); the change, the test and the measurements were prepared with Claude, then reviewed and submitted by jake-vc.
